story: Look up at the monument. In front of you stands El cocinero chino. This sculpture, created by Óscar Ortega, celebrates the immigration of Chinese people to Mexicali. It’s a tribute to the best Chinese cuisine in the world. A surprising fact: the sculpture cost approximately 10 million pesos. The Government of Baja California and private companies paid for it. It’s located at the entrance to La Chinesca, a neighborhood with a high concentration of Chinese residents. La Chinesca is a historic area where Chinese people have lived and worked since the beginning of the 20th century.

Name: El cocinero chino

La mejor cocina china del mundo.
Short description: monument in Mexicali, Mexico
Wikipedia (es): El cocinero chino es un monumento dedicado a la inmigración china a la ciudad de Mexicali, México. Es obra del escultor Óscar Ortega y fue inaugurada en 2025. Se encuentra en la entrada de la zona conocida como La Chinesca, en el cruce de las calles bulevar Adolfo López Mateos y la calle Juárez. La escultura de 23 metros de altura y hecha en concreto representa a un cocinero que sostiene en la mano izquierda una caja de comida china como homenaje a dicha gastronomía que se ha constituido como un referente cultural mexicalense. Tuvo un costo aproximado de 10 millones de pesos pagados por el Gobierno del Estado de Baja California y empresas privadas.

story: Look up at the towering structure before you. You stand in front of the Catedral de Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe, a place of worship dedicated to the Virgin of Guadalupe. It’s the cathedral, the seat of the Diocese of Mexicali, located in the city of Mexicali, the capital of Baja California. Nearby, you can see La Chinesca, a zone with a high concentration of residents of Chinese origin. This area, established in the early 20th century, was formed by Chinese immigrants brought from the United States to work the land. It’s estimated that 5,000 people live there today.
